catalog_quote: In her study of Metzontla Popoloca, Veerman-Leichsenring (1984, 1991) notes that stress, which is realized primarily as duration, falls on the penultimate syllable of a word. Stops and affricates are preglottalized, while liquids, approximants, and nasals are lengthened: /čàkū/ ‘fàce’ [čàʔkū]; /tīyé/ ‘night’ [tīyˑé] (page 21). With aspirated consonants, prenasalized consonants, and voiceless nasals, the consonants are essentially split, creating a phonetic sequence. When the syllable contains a long vowel or vowel sequence (including a vowel followed by a glottal stop), the vowel is long. In general, it is the consonant that shows the effects of accent, and with monosyllabic words, a prothetic vowel may appear (/kū/ ‘animal’ [ìʔkū] (page 22).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; it is cued mainly by duration, realised on the onset consonant of the stressed syllable (preglottalisation of stops and affricates, lengthening of sonorants; 'split' realisation of aspirated, prenasalised and voiceless-nasal consonants) rather than on the vowel, unless the syllable already has a long vowel/vowel sequence; monosyllabic words may take a prothetic vowel so that the stressed syllable is not word-final.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the survey passage.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllables: a prothetic vowel may appear (/kū/ 'animal' [ìʔkū]); no other exceptions given. The survey's page refs (21, 22) fall in ch. 2 'Fonologia' (pp. 20-52) of the 1991 grammar, so the primary statement should be there.
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for the word ('penultimate syllable of a word'); the survey passage is second-hand and says nothing about phrase-level or citation-form conditions. Tone (3 tonemes, ch. 3 of the grammar) is independent of stress per the survey's framing.
new_statements.identity_note: The 1984/1991 descriptions are of the Popoloca of Los Reyes Metzontla (Puebla), i.e. exactly mezo1235 [pbe] ('Southern Popoloca' together with San Juan Atzingo, poe, which is a separate glottocode). The survey statement is explicitly about 'Metzontla Popoloca'. Do not confuse with the Western Popoloca (San Felipe Otlaltepec, sanf1264) or Eastern Popoloca (Atzingo) stress descriptions by Williams & Pike 1968 and Kalstrom & Pike 1968, which are stem-final/penultimate-of-stem systems in other varieties.

sources.note: second-hand summary of Veerman-Leichsenring 1984/1991: stress in Metzontla Popoloca falls on the penultimate syllable of the word and is realised primarily as duration (preglottalisation of stops/affricates, lengthening of liquids/approximants/nasals; long vowels stay long; prothetic vowel in monosyllables), citing 'page 21' and 'page 22' of the grammar (= ch. 2 Fonologia, pp. 20-52, of the 1991 book).
